newsitem.title: UK: Path into Notts Forest cleared for Wray group.
newsitem.headline: Path into Notts Forest cleared for Wray group.

text.p: A consortium led by property developer Nigel Wray was the only bidder left in the battle for English soccer club Nottingham Forest on Monday after the 11th hour collapse of a rival group.

Forest shareholders will vote on the 19 million pound bid from Wray's Bridgford consortium at an Extraordinary General Meeting on Monday evening. The backing of 75 percent of the premier league club's 202 shareholders is required for the takeover to go ahead.
A consortium led by U.S. journalist Albert Scardino was forced out of the reckoning after the withdrawal of its main backer, Mercury Asset Management.
"We had to withdraw yesterday. Mercury scored an own goal," said Scardino.

Scardino said Mercury had told him on Friday evening that they had changed their view on the prospects for soccer clubs over the next two years or so. He said there had earlier been "no hint or suggestion" of the change of heart.
Scardino's attempts to resurrect the bid with the help of his two other backers, Electra Investment Trust and Nash Sells, failed to come to fruition this weekend.
Bridgford includes Wray, chairman of property group Burford and owner of Saracens rugby union club, author Phil Soar and former Tottenham Hostpur chairma Irving Scholar.

The consortium plans to pump 16 million pounds into the club to strengthen a squad battling against relegation. A total of some three million pounds will be available to shareholders who wish to take the cash while the consortium will also inherit debts estimated at around seven million pounds.
The group plans to float the club and are anxious for it to maintain its premier league status.
